description: CADS-dataset is a large-scale whole-body CT segmentation dataset containing 22,022 CT volumes with voxel-level annotations for 167 anatomical structures. It aggregates data from 40 diverse sources, including public archives, medical challenges, and newly contributed hospital cohorts, to support comprehensive whole-body anatomy segmentation.
name: CADS-dataset
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper describes annotation quality analysis through automated outlier detection of pseudo-labels in shape space using neural implicit functions, expert review of a significant portion of the unseen test set, and statistical ranking and selection among three model flavors using Dice and HD95 with significance testing. It also reports manual review of TotalSegmentator test annotations to classify labels as reliable or unreliable.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels were created by combining original ground-truth annotations from source datasets, additional manual annotations by three in-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist, registration-derived annotations for brain structures, interpolation of sparse slice annotations for SAROS, and large-scale pseudo-labeling across 22,022 CT scans. The pipeline includes shape-informed quality control, multi-strategy label optimization across GT-, Pseudo-, and Shape-flavor models, and replacement of pseudo-labels with original ground-truth annotations when available.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly discusses potential biases and limitations arising from fragmented data, limited anatomical coverage, single-source datasets, annotation inconsistencies, and systematic errors in existing public datasets such as missing costovertebral joints in rib annotations. It also notes that excluding low-quality pseudo-labels may remove pathological cases with atypical anatomy, potentially limiting learning of clinically important edge scenarios, and that facial regions in newly acquired head CT scans are intentionally anonymized, limiting detailed facial analysis.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset aggregates 22,022 CT volumes from 40 diverse sources, including large public archives such as TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, and AbdomenCT-1K; specialized annotation collections from medical imaging challenges and focused research studies; and newly contributed data including manual annotations on VISCERAL, 484 newly acquired anonymized head CTs, and 586 anonymized triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans. The collection spans over 100 medical centers across 16 countries and includes both healthy and pathological cases.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 79% of the initial collection does not include any manual annotations, and many of the annotated scans contain only partial annotations for one or a few structures. The dataset construction addresses this missing annotation coverage through pseudo-label generation and integration of partial and unlabeled scans.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data are volumetric CT scans collected from public repositories, medical imaging challenges, research archives such as TCIA, and newly acquired hospital cohorts. They include whole-body, head-and-neck, chest, abdomen, pelvis, and spine CT scans with varying imaging protocols, including contrast-enhanced and non-contrast acquisitions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes several limitations: exclusion of low-quality pseudo-labels may remove pathological cases with atypical anatomical variations; the dataset spans head to knees and does not yet cover additional regions such as hands and feet; some structures require refinement, including the brain mask, optic chiasm, heart, rectum, trachea, and vena cava; facial features in newly acquired head CTs are intentionally anonymized, limiting detailed facial analysis; and the modular multi-model design could be replaced by future unified architectures.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-collection manipulation includes whole-body pseudo-labeling of all scans, organization of 167 targets into nine anatomical groups, shape-based filtering that excludes the lowest-scoring 10% of pseudo-labels, ensemble label selection across GT-, Pseudo-, and Shape-flavor models, interpolation of sparse SAROS slice annotations into dense 3D annotations, head-region cropping to reduce false positives, and specialized rib refinement using connected-components analysis, vesselFM-based retrieval of costovertebral joints, morphological opening, size filtering, and nearest-rib assignment.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All images are reoriented to the standard RAS convention, resampled to 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, and their affine transformation matrices are simplified by removing rotation and translation components while preserving scaling and shear. For patient privacy in newly acquired hospital head CT scans, a Gaussian filter with σ = 5 voxels at 1.5 mm spacing is applied to facial regions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the dataset as supporting robust AI solutions in radiology, making comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers, and enabling clinical applications such as radiation therapy planning, diagnostic radiology, longitudinal organ tracking, personalized anatomical modeling, and large-scale population studies. It also notes privacy-related trade-offs from facial anonymization.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses include training whole-body CT segmentation models, anatomical landmark detection, cross-modality registration, anatomy-guided synthesis, radiation treatment planning, longitudinal organ tracking, personalized anatomical modeling, automated organ volume quantification, and large-scale population studies.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: The annotation pipeline uses nnU-Net specialized models for pseudo-label generation, neural implicit functions for shape-informed quality control, ANTS non-rigid transformation for registration-derived brain annotations, and vesselFM to retrieve tube-like structures for rib refinement.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains medical CT scans from hospital and public cohorts, including facial anatomy in head CT scans, pathological conditions, and clinical imaging from oncology patients. The paper states that newly acquired head CT facial regions were anonymized using Gaussian blurring for privacy.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: paper describes voxel-level segmentation labels but does not state a count of independent annotations per item
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: no demographic details of annotators are provided beyond roles such as medical research assistants and radiation oncologist
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: no annotation platform or software for creating labels is identified
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: paper does not describe imputing missing values; missing annotation coverage is handled via pseudo-labeling rather than value imputation
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: no versioning, update cadence, or maintenance commitment for the dataset is described
